citation.authors: Wu J, Hägg U, Rabie ABM
citation.title: Chinese norms of McNamara's cephalometric analysis

curation.notes: Compared 2026-10-08 (norms:compare a vs b exit 1, 22 differences, all in the source text; every mean, SD and n agreed). All 22 values re-read from the page images of Table 3 (p. 16, PDF p. 5) and Table 3 Extended (p. 17, PDF p. 6): agree. Decisions: (1) age band: both extractors gave the Table 1 ranges [11,13] (boys) and [11.9,13] (girls) → [12,12] for both sexes by merge-notes ruling ('12 y' → [12,12]); Table 1 ranges kept in each note. (2) source text normalised to 'Table 3, p. 16 (boys)' / 'Table 3 Extended, p. 17 (girls)'. (3) Co-A, Co-Gn, maxillomandibular difference: both 'same' → close. The merge notes asked to check b's flag: Wu's Fig. 1 legend (p. 14) defines condylion as the rearmost point on the condyle's outline; the catalogue's Co is the most posterior-superior point (catalogue appendix landmark table), so the definitions differ. (4) #31: printed −5.51/−3.83 stored + 90 (84.49/86.17), owner ruling 7 Oct; same (Wu's facial axis is PTM to constructed Gn against Ba-N, Table 2, as the catalogue). (5) incisor mm rows close (facial surface, Table 2), as both extractors. Scale not-stated with the 8.8% caveat (merge notes). Fix round 1 (2026-10-08, owner AGE-1 / MAL-1, rulings P42, P45, P47, review): ageBand [12,12] → [11,13] for both sexes from Table 1 (11.0-13.0 boys, 11.9-13.0 girls; completed years), owner AGE-1.

caveats: Film magnification 8.8% is stated (p. 14) but not whether values were corrected; assumed true size (owner ruling 8 Oct)

12-year-old southern Chinese schoolchildren, a partially stratified random sample from 10 Hong Kong schools (p. 13): occlusion was not selected, so this is an unselected population, not a Class I sample. Films from Cooke's 1984-85 oral health survey. Age (Table 1): boys 11.0-13.0 y (mean 12.4), girls 11.9-13.0 y (mean 12.5); entered as age band 11-13 for both sexes (owner AGE-1, 8 Oct; completed years, so 11.9 counts as 11).
Natural head posture (mirror 200 cm ahead) with ear-rods (p. 14). Hand traced, then digitised twice in CASSOS and averaged.
Condylion is the rearmost point on the condyle's outline (Fig. 1 legend, p. 14), not the catalogue's posterior-superior point: Co-A, Co-Gn and their difference are close.
Upper and lower incisor distances are measured from the facial surface (Table 2), not the tip: close (owner C1/M1).

Not entered: the 43 + 43 British Caucasian 12-year-olds in Hong Kong (Table 4) - a different population; Tables 5-6 (ethnic differences, comparison with McNamara 1984); medians, ranges and confidence intervals of Table 3.
